Ikwezi Lokusa Part 2

By: Tarryn Crossman | Paid

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
After our story aired in September so many viewers came forward and pledged to help the child at IL
One woman has managed to get 200 new mattresses, 200 pillows, clothes, toys and a team together to come and paint the dorms for the kids. The truck is being loaded in Bloem and then team are all heading to Mthatha to take real action for the kids at IL

Meanwhile the DOE appears to have done NOTHING
What we know is that they have received a budget sign off for the beds to be demolished, apparently they don't have a date for when this will happen.
The HOD of inclusive Ed says there is a team investigating the allegation of neglect by the staff, which will be complete next year.
But the people on the ground are saying nothing has changed, except the security on the campus. No-one is allowed in the dorms anymore. Apparently security are not letting any on or off with clearance from the principle.
The BSR guys have even been banned from going near the dorms.

I have a recorded telephone conversation with the spokesperson telling me that the HOD is taking it personally and his ego is bruised so no-one knows what is going on. But they are stonewalling us, because we 'offended him' according to the spokesperson. The MEC has been involved and they are having a big meeting on Monday, following which we will be given an update.

I am working on getting someone inside to film for us this weekend.

Script:


We first investigated Ikhwezi Lokusa, a government special needs boarding school in Mthatha, in the Eastern Cape, in 2018, exposing the children’s horrific living conditions.
They were sleeping in cold dormitories on beds made of bricks. The bathrooms were dilapidated and unsafe.
We’d been invited by the school's principal, as he wanted the Eastern Cape Department of Education to help the children

Ep 1
Claire and Archie Claire: if you had a child with CP, would you be happy that they came and attended this school
Archie: I would opt for another institution
Claire: that’s heartbreaking
Archie: yeah, but that’s the truth

In that first story, the Provincial Department of Education committed to fixing the problems, but never did.

Then, in September this year, we returned to Ikhwezi Lokusa, but this time the staff refused to let us film.

So, we used our cellphones to capture undercover footage. So disturbing was what we saw that it seemed to us a gross violation of human rights.

Vulnerable, mentally and physically disabled children dragging themselves naked across cold cement floors…. children forced to take care of other children

Horrified, we tried to find someone in charge. Unaware that we were filming, a supervisor told us our presence wouldn’t affect how the school operated.


SUPERVISOR
You are not going to change us. You are here working for Carte Blanche, we are going there.

We returned unannounced the next day to find no one looking after over 20 6-12-year-olds.

In fact, there wasn’t a care worker in sight for the close to 200 special needs children at Ikwezi Lokusa.

We wanted answers from the school's new principal.

GOVAN: Sorry, principal, please can I talk to you about
GOVAN: Principle, please
PRINCIPLE: I do not want to answer you. Do you want to make me cry

We later confronted the Head of Department for Inclusive Education in the Eastern Cape, Simon Ncapayi, showing him what we'd seen at Ikhwezi Lokusa

GOVAN ; Look at these videos of what we saw there. hese children are crawling around naked inside the facility at night.
DOE: Then who gave you access there?
G: Are you concerned about the condition of the children or the fact that we have these videos?
DOE: I am concerned about both

GOVAN AT HIS LAPTOP Bridge shot

After that story aired, we were inundated with messages from viewers and civic organisations wanting to help the children.

Whatsapp messages ping ping ping

Among them was Rozanne Marias, a Bloemfontein estate agent who watched the insert repeatedly.


ROZANNE
Look I must be frank - One watches many of these stories and wonders if you can make a difference, but where do you begin
I never thought I would get so far that we would end up here
That we would get the beds
That we would get the transport
Everything just fell into place


Rozanne, together with viewers from across the country, collected 200 mattresses, 200 pillows, toys, paints, clothes, and toiletries, and arranged a truck big enough to transport it all from Bloemfontein to Mthatha.

Govan and Rozanne
What was the hardest part for you
Getting the truck into the school

On the 19th of last month, we arrived in Mthatha with Rozanne, a team of volunteers and a truck full of donations. We’d planned to meet a delegation from the Eastern Cape Department of Education and their spokesperson, Malibongwe Mtima. It had taken weeks of planning, but the challenges were far from over.

Govan - We have arrived, the truck has been on the road for a full day and now they are struggling to open the gate.

Principle - go to the department and ask them to open for you

Despite Rozanne arranging for the gate to be open, we were now being told it wasn’t possible.


Eventually We were asked to move to a second gate.

Drive

But that, too, was locked and the school's security guards refused to let us in. (cut this visually)

Govan - the last time we were here, this gate was open and we were free to move through day and night

After a while, Ikhwezi Lokusa’s Deputy Principal arrived

Deputy - the department wants to go up the road so that they can meet you there

So, nearly two hours since arriving, we were again being told to wait. We tried the provincial department of educations spokesperson Mtima

MTIMA HANGS UP THE PHONE

He kept insisting someone was coming for us, before dropping the line. we repeatedly to called him back, but he never answered.

MTIMA VOICE MAIL

The team of volunteers was growing anxious as the driver could no longer be delayed. So, after being told the departmental delegation was waiting for us at yet another gate, we attempted to get there by navigating overhead power cables.

Power line - wo wo
Truck keeps driving

Unbelievably, the third gate was ALSO locked.

Govan calls Mtima
Mtima its Govan Whittle from Carte Blanche
No, I have sent people to you

The deputy principal made another appearance. But, having apparently been sent to help us, he departed soon after – locking the gate behind him.

Are you going to open for us
You not going to open
Aren’t you with the department
You not with the department

Having arrived at Ikhwezi Lokusa around 8:30 that morning we were eventually let in after midday. As the unloading began, we went in search of Mtima – who’d been inside the school the entire time.

Interview Mtima - confront 1

M- We never intentionally delayed your truck,
G - but you did the delay us
M - let me
G - We called you Mr. Tim, and you hung the phone up on us. We tried to call you back three more times. You didn't answer our call. And then you said you would send someone to us.
M - These this chaos just proves that these people and the colleagues that are here are not toeing the line.
G- Why did they say why they didn't do it?
M - all they have said was they could not explain themselves. That's why I say there's going to be legal recourse that is going to be taken because we can't afford this.

Meanwhile, a far better story was unfolding outside… a seemingly endless stream of donations was being unloaded from the truck.

Unpacking montage

Having worked so hard to make this moment happen, the stress was taking its toll on Rozanne.

Rozanne crying with Govan

Despite the challenges the team pushed ahead,------- delivering an early Christmas for the children of Ikwezi Lokusa

Natural audio where possible
45’ verite montage with Govan guns
And some of the volunteers
Try show rozanne - her and govan high fiving outside
Care workers looking at the toys with joy

Within hours, what were once depressing dormitories were transformed into inviting children's bedrooms – thanks to our dedicated Carte Blanche viewers.

Govan upsound from the room - maybe the car vroom - natural audio

Time running out, Rozanne led a team of painters into injecting some much-needed colour into the communal dining hall.

- 30’ painting montage - natural audio if possible
- interview beat why painting - I just wanted to add some colour of iets
- govan painting

Despite the improvements, we knew our efforts wouldn’t solve the more significant issues at the school. We confronted Mtima about what – if anything – had been done since our last investigation

subsequent to that. There's been numerous emails streaming, sweatshops and everything workshops.
G
Have any of the staff been taken to disciplinary process?
M
There are legal processes that we are undertaking because we do not want a situation where they do this and then at the end of the day, they get away with it

Despite being told that the beds would be demolished and replaced last month, there’d been no change to any of the infrastructure… not even a replaced toilet seat.

G
the department made promises to us. In 2018, we came back in 2023. Those promises were not implemented. Now we've come back two months later and you see nothing has been done.
M
There has been a process, a process that we are following that we started, for instance, to start with this and the issue of infrastructure. Mr..
G
To the infrastructure issues not getting attention. Mr. Cockburn said the beds would be demolished during the October holidays. That has not happened. Again, the department is making a promise.

M
We had the money, but the legalities we are not aware that this legalities are going to drag. We need to ensure that the landlord is aware so that when we demolish it does not take us to court.
G
So you didn't demolish the beds because you were afraid you might be legally obligated to rebuild the brick beds.

G
We've heard that after our broadcast of our previous story that people here were traumatized.
M
Yes. We were told that the way that we were colleagues, that that needed psychosocial support.
G
Staff were traumatized, not the children.
G
Thank you, Mr. Mortimer. It's been a dynamic and engaging interview. Good luck. Good luck on the on trying to solve the issues at the school. I have to promise you will be back

20’ verite build with natural audio

The reveal
Govans link Kids going crazy














PROMO ONE
VO: A story about change…
LINK GOVAN: This is you. This is every carte blanche viewer. You were horrified, but you took action…
VO: We return to the state-run boarding school for children with special needs - Ikhwezi lokusa - with a 12 wheeler truck filled with donations

PROMO TWO
VO: Locked out… disregarded … and made to wait for hours on end…
UPSOUND 00:33:53:22 - 00:34:14:20 – GOVAN - They behaved the way that they did because you vilified carte blanche and made us out to be the enemy, because we exposed the human rights violations being perpetrated against special needs children at the school.
VO: Despite the odds, a group of Carte Blanche viewers change the lives of vulnerable children in the Eastern Cape.


GOVAN CONFRONT
We called you Mr. Tim, and you hung the phone up on us. We tried to call you back three more times.

Interview or govan on the phone

VOICE OVER
we return to government special needs school Ikhwezi Lokusa to try and hand over donation to the children
But find ourselves locked out

Truck arriving driving
Govan in the car
Flicker lights
Black sign with flowers
Govan walking up to a locked gate


Mtima confront
- these people and the colleagues that are here are not toeing the line.
